Topic 3.7: READING Recognition

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on READING Recognition. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Recognize letters of the incorporated in children’s play to alphabet in lower case in and enhance letter recognition. out of class. •
2. Match upper case letters with • Learners could be guided to recognize corresponding lower case letters on walls, charts, cards and letters in class. labels to enhance letter recognition

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING RECOGNITION
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
READING Recognition helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING RECOGNITION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Recognize letters of the incorporated in children’s play to alphabet in lower case in and enhance letter recognition. out of class. •

What this means
In this part you learn to Recognize letters of the incorporated in children’s play to alphabet in lower case in and enhance letter recognition. out of class. •. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Recognize letters of the incorporated in children’s play to alphabet in lower case in and enhance letter recognition. out of class. •.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “READING Recognition”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Recognize letters of the incorporated in children’s play to alphabet in lower case in and enhance letter recognition. out of class. •. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Match upper case letters with • Learners could be guided to recognize corresponding lower case letters on walls, charts, cards and letters in class. labels to enhance letter recognition

What this means

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Match upper case letters with • Learners could be guided to recognize corresponding lower case letters on walls, charts, cards and letters in class. labels to enhance letter recognition.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about READING Recognition to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Match upper case letters with • Learners could be guided to recognize corresponding lower case letters on walls, charts, cards and letters in class. labels to enhance letter recognition. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what READING Recognition is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “READING Recognition”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: Recognize letters of the incorporated in children’s play to alphabet in lower case in and enhance letter recognition. out of class. •)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about READING Recognition to a partner. (skill: Match upper case letters with • Learners could be guided to recognize corresponding lower case letters on walls, charts, cards and letters in class. labels to enhance letter recognition)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach READING Recognition to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Recognize letters of the incorporated in children’s play to alphabet in lower case in and enhance letter recognition. out of class. •.
3. Practise this skill: Match upper case letters with • Learners could be guided to recognize corresponding lower case letters on walls, charts, cards and letters in class. labels to enhance letter recognition.
4. Make one local Kenya example of READING Recognition from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for READING Recognition: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study READING Recognition?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what READING Recognition means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Recognize letters of the incorporated in children’s play to alphabet in lower case in and enhance letter recognition. out of class. •.
5. Be able to: Match upper case letters with • Learners could be guided to recognize corresponding lower case letters on walls, charts, cards and letters in class. labels to enhance letter recognition.
